content:
eva: heads up — brought up model-y (int4v2) for long-context validation. on synthetic 64k prompts we see periodic phase jitter that produces small token perturbations and some off-by-one token repeats. looks different from the kv wrap cases we've chased before.

jared: can you paste the minimal repro and a short log? sounds like an interpolation artifact in the rotary table or the freq lookup.

eva: repro: `./longctx_runner --model model-y:int4v2 --prompt tests/64k_loop.json --rotary-scale 0.95 --kv_window 131072 --quant-profile int4v2 --seed 123`
log snippet (trimmed):
```
# sample tokens around pos 61440..61468
... "and then she" "and then she" "and then she" -> small repeats at 61456,61457
phase_lookup: pos=61456 -> idx=61456/stride -> table_idx=3835, frac=0.62
rot_sin[idx]=0.0234, rot_cos[idx]=0.9997
interp_sin = linear_interp(rot_sin[idx], rot_sin[idx+1], frac) -> 0.0238
# fp16 run uses higher-precision table, no repeats
```

sophia: interesting. so int4v2 kernel apparently uses a compact rotary table plus linear interpolation to save memory. That could introduce small phase discontinuities at higher positions where the table spacing is larger relative to frequency. The fp16 baseline probably computed sin/cos on the fly or used higher-res table.

omar: did we change the rotary index stride when switching to sharded KV? stride should be consistent but if kv sharding uses a different position map it can shift indices. Confirm kv_index_map for the run.

eva: kv_index_map looked contiguous; I dumped it: `/tmp/kv_map_1768800000.dump`. no sharding mismatch. The jitter correlates with table_idx boundaries (every ~16 positions).

jared: hypothesis: low-res sin/cos table + linear interpolation + quantized multiply (int4 accum path) -> roundoff that nudges logits enough for greedy sampling to flip for those tokens. Not classic wrap; smaller amplitude but still causes visible repeats.

sophia: agree. fixes to try:
- enable `rotary_table_highres=true` (runtime flag to use 4x table density)
- switch interpolation from linear -> cubic hermite (smoother)
- run kernel with accumulation in fp16 (even if inputs quantized) to see if numeric range is the issue

eva: ran quick experiments: 
- rotary_table_highres=true: repeats went away on the synthetic run
- cubic interp (local patch): also removed jitter but slightly slower
- accumulation in fp16: reduced but did not fully remove jitter (so interpolation/table density looks like dominant factor)

omar: good catch. we should add a short benchmark comparing table-resolutions and interpolation quality vs latency. If the highres table adds unacceptable memory, maybe we only enable highres for positions > training_window or for models with rotary_scale != 1.0.

jared: also add a unit test: run 70k positional sweep and diff tokens between fp16 baseline and quant kernels; if hamming distance > threshold, fail. Put that in onboarding/quant-smoke.

sophia: putting notes in the model onboarding checklist: "rotary table verification: compare lookup vs analytic sin/cos for pos up to kv_window; test interpolation modes; record table density used in quant builds."

eva: filed INF-8021 with repro, diffs, and artifacts: /artifacts/model-y/1768800000/. assigning to @eva for follow-up and @sophia for runtime patch. devx-bot will throttle incoming test traffic to the canary.

devx-bot: canary-throttle: set to 10% for slot 7. Created INF-8021 (https://redwood.internal/INF-8021).

jared: next steps:
1) add the highres-table toggle to runtime config and gate by model flag
2) land the unit test in onboarding harness
3) run A/B on small traffic with highres vs default and measure latency & memory impact

omar: FYI this is borderline with prior RoPE issues but materially different root cause. tagging eng-ml and eng-runtime so we don't conflate it with kv-wrap explorations.

eva: thanks all — i'll attach the numeric diffs and the mini-plot showing periodicity (every ~16 positions) to INF-8021. will update when A/B is done.
